clue.text: Advance amount of money in account to missing company

indicators.note: an account can be a spoken report, so the phrase is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: an advance is a loan, and an amount of money is a sum, giving the phrase loan sum

explanation.surface: Someone borrows against an account to cover a firm that has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in account' signals a homophone: LOAN SUM, said aloud, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lacking company feels lonely and solitary, which is the sense of the answer.

clue.text: Chimney rod made of backbone

parts.note: lum is a Scottish and northern English word for chimney
a bar is a rod of metal

explanation.surface: A chimney rod is made out of spine.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumbar describes the lower part of the spine, relating to the backbone.

clue.text: Latest song on radio gets total exposure

indicators.note: radio is heard not seen, so the phrase is pronounced

parts.note: the latest song is a new ditty

explanation.surface: A new hit played on the radio gets massive airplay.
explanation.walkthrough: NEW DITTY spoken quickly sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nudity is complete nakedness, total exposure of the body.

clue.text: Stop urge to snack

parts.note: to scotch is to stop or put an end to
to egg on is to urge

explanation.surface: Resist the craving to eat between meals.
explanation.walkthrough: A Scotch egg is a British snack: a boiled egg wrapped in sausage meat and breadcrumbs.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scotch egg is a picnic snack, an example of the category.

clue.text: Verbally grades stock with Queen's old jesters

indicators.note: verbally means spoken aloud, so the word for grades is heard

parts.note: marks are grades awarded
broth is soup stock
ER, Elizabeth Regina, with the possessive s

explanation.surface: Grading soup stock aloud alongside the monarch's former court fools.
explanation.walkthrough: MARKS sounds like MARX; the Marx Brothers were American film comedians.
explanation.definitionFit: The Marx Brothers were a family of comic performers from the old days of film, jesters in effect.

clue.text: Bad luck to have head covering its heart

parts.note: a hood is a covering for the head
the middle two letters of the head covering just found, hood

explanation.surface: Wearing a hat over your heart is said to bring misfortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its' points back to the head covering, so its heart is the middle pair of HOOD.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoodoo is a jinx or run of misfortune, a synonym for bad luck.

clue.text: Literary madame's guillotined for her organ

indicators.note: guillotined means beheaded, so the first letter goes

parts.note: Madame Bovary is Flaubert's novel heroine

explanation.surface: A French heroine of fiction is beheaded for her musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guillotined' takes the head (B) off BOVARY.
explanation.definitionFit: The ovary is a female reproductive organ, hence her organ.

clue.text: Every 24 hours, nurse shortly switches one with a medical procedure

indicators.note: one is I, and the I trades places with the letter A

parts.note: daily means every day, each 24 hours

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the end of the word goes

parts.note: sister is a senior nurse in Britain

explanation.surface: A nurse changes shift every day to help with a hospital treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping I and A turns DAILY into DIALY; SISTER shortened gives SIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Dialysis is a medical procedure filtering the blood when kidneys fail.

clue.text: Beaten, one's a bit deferential

indicators.note: beaten means battered out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Defeated, someone becomes a little submissive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beaten' rearranges ONESABIT into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeisant means showing obeisance or respect, a synonym for deferential.

clue.text: Dormice developed tail of twice average

indicators.note: developed as in changed into a new form, so the letters of the rodents' name are reworked
the tail of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Some dormice grew a tail twice as long as normal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges DORMICE into MEDIOCR, and 'tail of' adds E, the last letter of 'twice'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mediocre means middling or ordinary, a synonym for average in its dismissive sense.

clue.text: Destructive effect of a sign that's made in anger

indicators.note: the letters for a sign are placed inside the word for anger

parts.note: rage is fury or anger
V for the V-sign, a rude British hand gesture

explanation.surface: A rude hand gesture made in a temper has destructive consequences.
explanation.walkthrough: The V-sign is a British insult made with two fingers; 'that's made' is link material.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravages, or ravage, is the damage wrought by something destructive, as in the ravage of war.

clue.text: Desperate guy came up with sword swallowing in medieval pageant

parts.note: Desperate Dan is a British comic-strip character from The Dandy

indicators.note: one word swallows another, taking it inside

parts.note: a sabre is a curved sword

indicators.note: in a down clue up means reading bottom to top

explanation.surface: A frantic man arrived with a blade being swallowed at a medieval show.
explanation.walkthrough: Desperate Dan is a hugely strong cowboy in a British children's comic; 'up' reverses only the word for arrived, which then sits inside the blade.
explanation.definitionFit: The danse macabre, or dance of death, was a medieval allegorical procession.

clue.text: Room with window that doesn't open or close

indicators.note: a word with no opening or closing letter loses its first and last letters

parts.note: a lattice is a window of criss-crossed strips

explanation.surface: A room has a window that is permanently shut.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a fixed window; instead LATTICE loses its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An attic is a room in the roof space of a house.

clue.text: Federation of German Industry's said they're watching you?

indicators.note: said signals the letters are to be pronounced aloud

parts.note: BDI is the Bundesverband der Deutschen Industrie, the Federation of German Industry, with 's added

explanation.surface: German industrialists are rumoured to be keeping an eye on you.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken as letters, B-D-I's comes out like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Small bright eyes that watch closely and suspiciously are called beady eyes.

clue.text: Ropes knotting, meeting and getting back

indicators.note: knotting twists ropes about, so their letters are tangled into a new order

parts.note: a session is a meeting of a body

explanation.surface: Tying ropes at a meeting before retrieving something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meeting' looks like part of the surface about ropes, but it simply supplies the second half.
explanation.definitionFit: Repossession is the taking back of goods by a lender, so it is a getting back.

clue.text: Masses' advice to the overweight?

definitions.meaning: a large quantity, a great many
read as two words, an instruction to lose weight

explanation.definitionFit: Shedloads is slang for a great quantity, while shed loads tells the heavy to drop weight.

clue.text: Star sign that's vulnerable without independent directions

indicators.note: without as outside, so one word wraps round other letters
independent here says each compass letter goes into the word for vulnerable on its own, separately

parts.note: at risk means vulnerable
S for south, a compass direction
E for east, a second compass direction

explanation.surface: An astrological sign said to be exposed and lost.
explanation.walkthrough: The two compass letters are not inserted as a pair: each goes in at its own place, giving A-S-T-E-RISK.
explanation.definitionFit: An asterisk is a typographic star, a sign printed as a star.

clue.text: Bent nib's instrumental to this song

parts.note: a nib is a pen point, standing for a pen
a chant is a song

explanation.surface: A crooked nib plays its part in this song.
explanation.definitionFit: A penchant is a liking or inclination, a bent for something.

clue.text: One pretending to be occupied with shelf for big tool

indicators.note: one word is filled, or occupied, by another placed inside it

parts.note: a shammer is someone who shams or pretends
a ledge is a narrow shelf

explanation.surface: A fraud is busy putting up a shelf and needs a hefty implement.
explanation.definitionFit: A sledgehammer is a large heavy hammer, a big tool.

clue.text: Jack could be this officer

definitions.meaning: a jack is a flag on a ship, an example of a naval flag

explanation.definitionFit: An ensign is both a flag flown on ships, of which a jack is one, and a junior officer.

clue.text: Trial by fire or wood

parts.note: deal is pine or fir timber

explanation.surface: Testing guilt by burning or by timber.
explanation.walkthrough: Medieval trial by ordeal included ordeal by fire.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a severe test, historically a trial by fire or water.

clue.text: No kind of confidence trick is unnaturally odd

indicators.note: no here says the letters of the following words are absent from the mix
unnaturally means in a distorted way, so the remaining letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these words form the pool
these letters are taken out of the pool

explanation.surface: A con that is no ordinary trick seems strangely peculiar.
explanation.walkthrough: Take KINDOF out of CONFIDENCETRICK; 'unnaturally' rearranges the remaining nine letters into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Eccentric means unconventional or strange, a synonym for odd.

clue.text: Unaffected by rising water?

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means reading upwards

parts.note: Evian is a brand of mineral water

explanation.surface: Someone untouched by a flood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns EVIAN upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Naive means artless and natural, a synonym for unaffected.

clue.text: Content to feel unaroused by satellite

definitions.note: used adjectivally: belonging to the moon, Earth's satellite

indicators.note: the contents of a phrase are the letters held within it

explanation.surface: Feeling calm and unexcited while watching the moon on TV.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'feeL UNARoused'; 'by' is link material.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunar means relating to the moon, which is Earth's natural satellite.

clue.text: Rightly inclined to get one's powder over one

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral; one's powder is I followed by its powder

indicators.note: over here means covering, so one piece sits around another

parts.note: talc is talcum powder
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Someone gets their powder sprinkled over them.
explanation.walkthrough: I, then TALC wrapped over a second I.
explanation.definitionFit: Italic type slopes to the right, so it is inclined in that direction.

clue.text: A warrior holding back is harsh

indicators.note: one word holds another within it

parts.note: a brave is a Native American warrior

indicators.note: back means the little word is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A fighter who is holding back is rough-edged.
explanation.walkthrough: A brave is the traditional English term for a Native American fighter; 'back' reverses only the little word before 'is harsh'.
explanation.definitionFit: Abrasive means grating or rough, a synonym for harsh.

clue.text: What to wear after being dressed up to the nines to produce litter?

parts.note: kit is clothing, the gear one wears

parts.words: after being dressed up to the nines
parts.note: the number coming straight after nine is ten

explanation.surface: Getting dressed up to the nines for some reason produces rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Dressed up to the nines suggests smart clothes; instead ten is what comes after the nines.
explanation.definitionFit: To kitten is a verb meaning to give birth to a litter of kittens.

clue.text: Own most of woolly fabric that's about

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the pieces are read backwards
most of a word drops its last letter

parts.note: lanose is a botanical word for woolly
rep is a ribbed fabric

explanation.surface: Most of a woolly material belongs to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Lanose is a rare botanical word for woolly; 'that's about' reverses the whole string, not just the fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Personal means belonging to oneself, as in one's own property.
